title: Trace partition ownership and regional failure
description: Select a scenario to see which path is active, where request units are consumed, and why a healthy account can still throttle one hot partition key range.

nodes.label: Cosmos SDK client
nodes.detail: Caches account topology, sends the partition key with point operations, carries session tokens, and retries documented transient responses with bounded backoff.

nodes.label: Account endpoint
nodes.detail: Resolves the request to a region and partition key range. A preferred-regions policy should match the application's failover contract.

nodes.label: Region A
nodes.detail: Hosts replicated partition key ranges and receives the full configured regional RU/s budget.

nodes.label: Hot key range
nodes.detail: One physical partition receives a disproportionate share of requests. Other partitions can be idle while this range returns 429 responses.

nodes.label: Region B
nodes.detail: Maintains replicated data and can receive traffic when routing changes or the preferred region is unavailable.

nodes.label: Other key ranges
nodes.detail: Evenly distributed logical partitions retain capacity that cannot automatically rescue a single overloaded key range.

scenarios.label: Balanced session reads
scenarios.summary: The client routes by partition key to Region A, and requests are spread across key ranges.
scenarios.result: Session consistency preserves the client's session guarantees while balanced keys let physical partitions consume their regional RU budget independently.

scenarios.label: Hot partition
scenarios.summary: Most requests target one logical key family even though total account RU/s still has headroom.
scenarios.result: The hot range can return 429 responses while other ranges remain quiet. Increase key cardinality or redesign ownership before simply adding more account-level RU/s.

scenarios.label: Regional read
scenarios.summary: A client near Region B reads from its preferred replica region under a relaxed consistency contract.
scenarios.result: Local reads reduce network distance. The selected consistency level still defines freshness and ordering; proximity does not strengthen the contract.

scenarios.label: Preferred region fails
scenarios.summary: Region A is unavailable and the client refreshes topology before routing supported operations to Region B.
scenarios.result: Availability depends on the configured write-region mode, consistency, SDK region preferences, and application retry policy. Drill the exact account configuration rather than assuming every operation fails over identically.
